questions.q: Different varieties of the same gene are called
questions.solution:
An allele is a variant of a gene controlling the same trait and occupying a specific region on a chromosome (called the locus).
One famous example of how alleles work is the alleles responsible for the flower colour in garden peas. The colour of garden peas flowers can be either purple or white. The gene coding for this trait, responsible for producing a purple pigment, is found in two forms, allele for purple colour and allele for white colour.
(This was one of the seven traits studied by Gregor Mendel in his experiments that later established the principles of genetics.)

questions.q: Chlorine occurs in nature in two isotopic forms of masses 35 u and 37 u in the ratio of $3: 1$ respectively. What is the average atomic mass of the Chlorine atom?
questions.solution:
The isotopes of chlorine are in the ratio $3: 1$.
Therefore, in any sample of chlorine, ${ }_{17}^{35} \mathrm{CI}$ will constitute $75 \%$ and ${ }_{17}^{35} \mathrm{CI}$ will constitute $25 \%$.
The proportion in which the isotopes are found in nature is always constant.
Therefore, in a sample of chlorine, the average atomic mass would be,
The average atomic mass of chlorine
$\begin{aligned}
& =\left(\frac{35 \times 75}{100}\right)+\left(\frac{37 \times 25}{100}\right) \\
& =\frac{105}{4}+\frac{37}{4}=\frac{142}{4} \\
& =35.5 \mathrm{u}
\end{aligned}$
The average atomic mass of chlorine is equal to 35.5 u .

We define the power of a lens as the reciprocal of the focal length of the lens. So, the power of the lens is expressed as $\mathrm{P}=1 / \mathrm{f}$
Where $f$ is the focal length and is expressed in meters. So, the unit of power of the lens is expressed in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$. This is also expressed as diopter.
As we know that the focal length of a convex lens is taken as in positive sign and the focal length of a concave lens is taken negatively. So, the power of a convex lens is positive, and the power of a concave lens is negative.
In this question, it is given that the lens is convex, and its focal length is 25 cm . First, we will convert the focal length into meters.
$\Rightarrow 25 \mathrm{~cm}=0.25 \mathrm{~m} \Rightarrow 25 \mathrm{~cm}=0.25 \mathrm{~m}$
Now, substituting the value of focal length in the formula of power of lens we get
$\begin{aligned}
& P=\frac{1}{0.25} \mathrm{~m}^{-1} \\
& \Rightarrow P=4 \mathrm{~m}^{-1}
\end{aligned}\mathrm{m}-1$ is also expressed as diopters or $D$
As it is a convex lens so its power is positive.
Thus, the power of the lens is +4 D .

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a feature of the Constitution of India?
options: It provides a set of basic rules.
It specifies the power of the Government.
It is the supreme law of the land.
It specifies the supremacy of the judiciary.
questions.solution: In India, the constitutional supremacy was explicitly reiterated in the Minerva Mills case whereby the Supreme Court held that "government, legislature, executive and judiciary are all bound by the Constitution, and nobody, is above or beyond the Constitution." Every law made by the parliament is subject to interpretation by Supreme Court in the light of ideals and objectives of the constitution and if they go beyond or above that, they can be held null and void. Indian Constitution does not have the express provision of separation of judicial and parliamentary supremacy but it's not quite unclear also. It is the prerogative of the parliament to amend the constitution and make the laws; it is the duty of the judiciary to decide if the basic structure of the constitution are transgressed by such laws. Thus, we can say that the constitution does not specify the supremacy of the judiciary.

questions.q: For what value of $\theta$, where $0 \lt \theta \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$, does $\sin \theta+\sin \theta\cos \theta$ attain maximum value?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Let } S=\sin \theta+\sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta \\ & \frac{d s}{d \theta}=\cos \theta+\cos ^2 \theta-\sin ^2 \theta \\ & =2 \cos ^2 \theta+\cos \theta-1=0 \\ & =(\cos \theta+1)(2 \cos \theta-1)=0 \\ & \therefore \cos \theta \neq 1 \therefore \cos \theta=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{3}\end{aligned}$
Now, $\frac{d^2 s}{d \theta^2}=-4 \cos \theta \sin \theta-\sin \theta\left(\frac{d^2 s}{d \theta^2}\right)_{\left(x=\frac{\pi}{3}\right)}=-4 \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \lt 0\therefore$ function is maximum at $x=\frac{\pi}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of $f(x)=|x|-1$ :
1. $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1$.
2. $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x=0$.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Here, $f(x)=|x|-1\therefore f(x)\left\{\begin{array}{cc}
-x-1, & x \lt 0 \\
x-1, & x \geq 0
\end{array}\right.$
For continuity at $x=1$.
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{LHL}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{-}}(x-1)=1-1=0 \\
& \mathrm{RHL}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{+}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{+}}(x-1)=1-1=0
\end{aligned}\therefore f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1$.
For differentiability at $x=0$.
$\begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime}(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}
-1, & x \lt 0 \\
1, & x \geq 0
\end{array}\right. \\
& \mathrm{LHD}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} f^{\prime}(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}}(-1)=-1 \\
& \mathrm{RHD}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} f^{\prime}(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}(1)=1
\end{aligned}\therefore f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x=0$

questions.q:
Let $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}1+\frac{x}{2 k}, & 0 \lt x \lt 2 \\ k x, & 2 \leq x \lt 4\end{array}\right.$
If $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} f(x)$ exists, then what is the value of $k$ ?
questions.solution:
$f(x)= \begin{cases}1+\frac{x}{2 k}, & 0 \lt x \lt 2 \\ k x, & 2 \leq x \lt 4\end{cases}$
Hence, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} f(x)$ exists so we can write that
$\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}} f(x) \\
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{-}}\left(1+\frac{x}{2 k}\right)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}}(k x) \\
& \Rightarrow 1+\frac{2}{2 k}=2 k \\
& \Rightarrow 1+\frac{1}{k}=2 k \\
& \Rightarrow k+1=2 k^2 \\
& \Rightarrow 2 k^2-k-1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 2 k^2-2 k+k-1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 2 k(k-1)+1(k-1)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow(2 k+1)(k-1)=0 \\
& \therefore k=1 \text { or } k=-\frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}$
